items.name: EC2 Node Types
items.text: Primary (YARN/HDFS; 3 for HA). Core runs tasks + HDFS (On-Demand). Task is compute-only (Spot). Fleets mix types; groups use one.

items.name: Cluster Lifecycle
items.text: Transient clusters run batch steps then terminate. Long-running clusters use managed scaling (YARN metrics) and auto-termination.

items.name: EMR Tooling
items.text: Bootstrap actions configure nodes at launch. Steps run jobs (ActionOnFailure). EMR Studio hosts notebooks; logs archive to S3 URI.

items: Avoid Spot on core nodes (HDFS loss risk)—use Spot on task nodes. HDFS is ephemeral; store data of record in S3.
'Least operational overhead' favors Glue or EMR Serverless over EMR on EC2 unless custom frameworks/tuning are needed.
Debug failed steps on terminated clusters via the S3 log URI (cluster, step, and YARN logs) or Spark history server.
Use Glue Data Catalog as Hive metastore to share tables with Athena/Glue. TB-scale log processing often points to EMR.
